(4) Check docs/status/requirement_status.yaml and docs/requirements.yaml for staleness -- REQ-033 should currently show status in_progress with no done event yet.

result.summary:
Independently re-verified REQ-033 (Letflow.Definitions.SnapshotStore) end to end -- did not trust TEST-RUNNER's report (test/reports/report-2026-08-17-WF02-REQ033-20260817.yaml) or REVIEWER's Step 2d self-report; re-ran everything and re-read the actual code/tests myself.

(1) mix test independently re-run on this host (git branch feature/WF02-REQ033-20260817, clean working tree except this handoff file) against the real docker-compose Postgres (letflow-postgres-1, confirmed `docker compose ps` Up/healthy). `mix test --seed 1` (full suite): exit code 0, verbatim summary line '4 properties, 427 tests, 0 failures', 'Finished in 14.8-14.9 seconds'. Ran it twice (once observed live, once redirected to /tmp/rv_test_full.log with $? captured directly, avoiding the pipe-to-tail exit-code trap) -- both times exit 0, both times 427/4/0, matching TEST-RUNNER's claimed 427 tests/4 properties/0 failures exactly, not merely 'close enough'. Isolated re-run of the requirement's own file, `mix test test/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store_test.exs`: exit 0, '16 tests, 0 failures', matching TEST-RUNNER's isolated count. Also ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force`: clean, 48 files, no warnings.

(2) Each of REQ-033's 5 acceptance_criteria (docs/requirements.yaml lines ~1548-1553) checked individually against the actual current code (lib/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store.ex) and tests (test/letflow/definitions/snapshot_store_test.exs), not against the design doc's paraphrase or the test report's summary:
  AC1 (create/2 on a valid definition_id inserts a snapshot whose graph matches the source row at call time) -- satisfied. create/3's locked-read-then-insert-then-reselect path (snapshot_store.ex L118-215) copies name/version/graph directly off the FOR-SHARE-locked process_definitions row. Test 'create/3 inserts a snapshot row whose graph, name and version match the source process_definitions row' (test file L120-154) uses a distinctive, non-default graph and asserts equality both on the immediate return value and on a fresh re-select from Postgres. PASS.
  AC2 (create/2 twice with same instance_id is idempotent no-op OR returns a distinct SnapshotAlreadyExists-equivalent error -- pick one, state which in the moduledoc) -- satisfied, and the moduledoc-must-state-the-choice sub-requirement specifically confirmed: moduledoc's '## `create/3` is idempotent on `instance_id`' section (snapshot_store.ex L16-28) explicitly states the idempotent-no-op reading was chosen, WHY (an S3 EE-01 retry after a crash/timeout needs convergence without its own error-classification logic), and explicitly acknowledges the ambiguity this creates (can't tell whether a call created or found the row) as deliberate, not an oversight. This is a real stated choice, not code whose behavior merely happens to be idempotent with no documentation of intent. Code matches: on_conflict: :nothing / conflict_target: :instance_id (L201-204) with insert-then-reselect-by-PK (L206-210), no changeset-error path exercised on a same-id retry. Test 'a second create/3 call with the SAME instance_id and SAME definition_id returns the pre-existing snapshot, inserts zero additional rows' (L177-193) confirms via snapshotted_at identity (proving no second real insert) and a row-count assertion. PASS.
  AC3 (get_by_instance_id/1 on an instance_id with no snapshot returns a not-found error, not nil) -- satisfied. get_by_instance_id/2 (L138-146) pattern-matches Repo.get's nil into {:error, :snapshot_not_found} explicitly, never returning nil to the caller. Test (L248-257) asserts the exact tuple AND `refute is_nil(result)` explicitly, plus a companion 'finds a snapshot created by create/3' positive-path test. PASS.
  AC4 (deleting a process_definitions row a snapshot references is rejected as foreign_key_violation, snapshot remains present/unmodified, no ON-DELETE-CASCADE side effect) -- satisfied. Verified the actual migration, not just the requirement's prose: priv/repo/migrations/20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs L93-96, `references(:process_definitions, ..., on_delete: :nothing)` -- confirmed no CASCADE. Test 'deleting a process_definitions row referenced by a snapshot raises Ecto.ConstraintError ... and the snapshot survives, byte-for-byte' (L284-315) does a real Repo.delete/2 against the source row inside assert_raise Ecto.ConstraintError, checks the exception message names the actual fkey constraint (instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey), then re-fetches the snapshot afterward and asserts full struct equality (not just 'still exists') against the pre-delete struct, plus confirms the process_definitions row itself is untouched. This is SnapshotStore-adjacent (the FK itself is REQ-027's, not new code here), correctly noted as such in the test's own describe block, and REQ-033 still owns proving the guarantee holds through its own code path. PASS.
  AC5 (moduledoc explicitly states the EE-01 instance-start integration point is S3 scope, not built here) -- satisfied. Moduledoc's '## S3 scope boundary' section (L8-14) states this in as many words: 'Calling create/3 at instance-start time -- before any event is appended (EE-01) -- is S3 scope, not built here. The engine that would make that call doesn't exist in Letflow yet.' Test 'SnapshotStore's moduledoc states EE-01/instance-start integration is S3 scope, not built here' (L326-338) fetches the compiled moduledoc via Code.fetch_docs/1 (not the source file's raw text -- proves the doc actually ships in the compiled artifact) and asserts on the exact substrings 'EE-01', 'S3 scope, not built here', 'instance-start'. PASS.

All 5 ACs independently confirmed satisfied by the current code and tests, not by the test report's or REVIEWER's self-description of them.

(3) REVIEWER's Step 2d judgment call (handoffs/WF02-REQ033-20260817/step-02d-reviewer.json) on the differing-definition_id retry: REVIEWER confirmed as acceptable-as-built that a create/3 retry for the same instance_id with a DIFFERENT definition_id is silently discarded (first-writer-wins, no error) since ON CONFLICT (instance_id) DO NOTHING has no natural comparison point for the other columns, and made a non-blocking recommendation that TEST-DESIGNER pin this exact behavior in a test. Confirmed both halves landed, not silently dropped: (a) TESTED -- 'a second create/3 call with the SAME instance_id but a DIFFERENT definition_id is silently discarded -- the original snapshot is returned unchanged, no error' (test file L195-239) is exactly REVIEWER's recommended case: two distinct process_definitions rows with distinguishable graphs/versions, asserts the retry does not error/raise, does not adopt the second definition_id's identity, only one row total is ever written, and a fresh re-select confirms the first definition's data persisted. (b) DOCUMENTED, not silently dropped -- the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req033-snapshot-store.md) states this explicitly as OQ-2 (S9, lines ~504-517): names the exact mechanism, the caller-bug risk, and explicitly distinguishes it from REQ-025's tenant_id precedent (the reasoning REVIEWER's own Step 2d sign-off independently re-derived and agreed with, rather than citing the design doc as having already settled it). The moduledoc's 'Open questions carried from the design, not resolved here' section (L80-85) names OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-3 explicitly and points to the design doc for the full reasoning rather than silently omitting them. This is adequately reflected -- not spelled out a third time verbatim inside the idempotency section itself, but present, named, and traceable across design doc -> moduledoc -> test -> REVIEWER sign-off, which satisfies 'not silently dropped'.

(4) Staleness check: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-033 entry (line ~1518) currently reads `status: in_progress`, not done -- correct, DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet. docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (grepped for '- req: REQ-033') has exactly one event, 'started' at 2026-08-17T13:24:35Z by ORCH, and no 'done' event anywhere in the file for REQ-033 -- correct, matches the expected pre-DOC-UPDATER state exactly, no staleness found in either file.

No blocking issues found. TEST-RUNNER's PASS report is corroborated by independent re-execution, not merely copied.
